clue.text: Manager protects a number showing emaciation

indicators.note: to protect is to surround and shield, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a boss is a manager
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A manager shields one figure, perhaps a starving worker, in a grim office scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Emaciation leaves a person thin to the point that the skeleton shows, a state of extreme bony thinness.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to expire is to end

explanation.surface: A girl's support is about to run out.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female forename, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Nobleman arrives in New York? Almost!

indicators.note: to arrive in a place is to be within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A peer has very nearly reached New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are synonyms meaning not quite.

clue.text: The first person in the body of the church is unworldly

indicators.note: in places the first-person pronoun inside the church word

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: A churchgoer sitting in the main aisle is innocent of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and inexperienced, lacking worldly wisdom.

clue.text: Reckoning to eat fowl — part of the breast

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: a sum is a reckoning or calculation
a tern is a seabird, loosely a fowl

explanation.surface: Working out how much fowl to eat, specifically the breast meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone, the flat bone in the middle of the chest.

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaning lady
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A cleaner is put to work running a ferry service.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Charon rows the dead across the Styx; CHAR is the British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the boatman who carries souls of the dead across the river Styx to Hades.

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Claire, a medic, is a rebel in her profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the doctor' looks like Claire's job title; 'doctor' is the anagram signal and 'the' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretical view departs from accepted doctrine, as a dissident's does.

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British Army soldiers
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A soldier is handed a drink in exchange for a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper correspondent is a journalist who reports news from a place.

clue.text: Partiality gets me in post improperly

indicators.note: done improperly means arranged wrongly, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Favouritism lands the speaker a job they should not have.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring relatives or friends in appointments is a form of unfair partiality.

clue.text: Judge returned hand tool to prospector

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an axe is a tool wielded by hand
a miner digs for minerals, like a prospector

explanation.surface: A judge gives back a hand tool to a gold prospector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like the subject doing the returning; it is the definition, and 'returned' turns the tool's name around.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner assesses and judges candidates or work, as a judge assesses an entry.

clue.text: Catch out Tory leader and remove

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the word Tory

parts.note: to rip up something is to tear it out and remove it

explanation.surface: A political scene: someone catches out the Conservative leader and gets rid of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip someone up is an idiom for catching them in an error or inconsistency.

indicators.note: sounds signals a word said aloud matching another spelling

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: Is flying high going to hurt?
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to rise and glide at a great height, like a bird.

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An editor reworks a novel in order to investigate something.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve into a subject is to investigate it deeply, which is to probe it.

definitions.note: the plural refers to the deck of cards collectively

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the letter

parts.note: a tart remark is a scathing one
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Clairvoyants are disparaging about an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TART round O. The definition treats the whole pack of cards as the 'tellers'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarot pack is a set of cards used by readers to predict someone's future.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A cat described as tiny, a kitten perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element is proverbially the tiniest thing there is.

clue.text: Hose gets Kitty in an awkward situation

parts.note: hose is a word for stockings or tights
a kitty is a pot of shared money

explanation.surface: A cat tangled in stockings is stuck in a predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hose; it is legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a difficult or awkward situation that is hard to escape.

definitions.meaning: a court game played with a hard ball, ancestor of squash

explanation.surface: Crooked schemes surround some sport, as in match-fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is just a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: dishonest schemes, and the court game related to squash.

clue.text: Drinks held dear in French coaches

indicators.note: held means contained, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: teas are drinks
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Drinks are kept in French buses.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach is to instruct, so coaches are people who teach.

clue.text: Give gear out? That'll cause distress!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Handing out equipment will upset someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to upset them or give them a sense of injury.

definitions.meaning: busy, as a telephone line or toilet in use

explanation.surface: Someone has pledged to be busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrothed couples are pledged to wed; a line in use is busy: two senses of one word.

definitions.meaning: made of fir or pine planks; the noun is used attributively
to cope with or manage something

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a softwood timber, and to deal with something is to handle it.

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for 'has'
full means complete, all of it

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie's complete name is asked for.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to name them, as in 'they call him Bob'.

clue.text: Bed to deteriorate after time in country home

indicators.note: after places the earlier pieces before the final one

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
to age is to decline with time

explanation.surface: A bed left to decay for years in a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A small house in the country, typically a rural dwelling.

clue.text: Type of pottery made with Barium compound

parts.note: Ba is the chemical symbol for barium
a salt is a chemical compound

explanation.surface: A ceramic glaze is made from a barium compound.
explanation.walkthrough: Wedgwood's black stoneware is called basalt ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Black basalt is an unglazed stoneware made by Wedgwood, named after the volcanic rock.

indicators.note: taking means swallowing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a baker is a cook
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tumbler is falling over because a chef is on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tumbler' suggests an acrobat; it is a drinking cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a drinking cup without a stem, like a tumbler.

clue.text: Proofreader's mark shows concern with the letter "t"

parts.note: care is concern or worry
taken as the letter itself

explanation.surface: A proofreader marks a worry about a single letter t.
explanation.definitionFit: The small inverted V proofreaders put in a text to show where something should be inserted.

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the following words

parts.note: something last-minute is late
a tern is a seabird, a winged thing

explanation.surface: A football winger is brought on as a late substitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests football, but it is a seabird; 'in' puts it inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To alternate is to switch back and forth between two things in turn.

clue.text: Health hazard creates fuss among sailors

indicators.note: among means amid, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, sailors
ado is fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A safety risk causes commotion on board ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A radioactive gas seeping from the ground is a cause of lung cancer, a threat to wellbeing.

parts.note: ex- means former or old

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to drain is to empty

explanation.surface: Waste is discharged from an old drain that was severed.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to release or discharge them from a duty or obligation.

parts.note: a land is a country
Mark is one of the four Gospel writers

explanation.surface: A national evangelist marks a turning point in a nation's history.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark event is a milestone, a significant turning point in history.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
heat is intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: Someone hushes a lawyer about a crime of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting cover, as for a sword or knife blade, is a protective case.

clue.text: Smirk when taking in this month in Irish province

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a leer is a sly or knowing smirk
inst., short for instant, means of this month in old business letters

explanation.surface: Someone smirks while visiting an Irish province this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST (instant) is a dated commercial abbreviation for 'of the current month'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four traditional provinces of Ireland, in the east, containing Dublin.
